commit.message:
multi: gate BOLT 12 offers behind a protocol flag

The database builder opens the offer store only when the protocol flag is
set. The offer table is a development migration, which a release build
does not apply, and the runtime is behind --protocol.bolt12-offers, which
only a dev build has.

At startup the node refuses the flag unless it runs native SQL with
onion messages and route blinding, and the offer migration is part of
the build. A misconfigured node therefore fails at once, not on the
first offer.

bolt12handler: add the invoice request handler

Accept an incoming invoice request, resolve it against the offer store,
check it against the offer it names, and reply with a generated invoice
over the sender's reply path.

itest: assert restored sweep spends its input

Carol's sweep can be replaced after the mempool snapshot and before a
block is mined. The exact transaction-ID assertion then rejects a valid
claim during force-close backup recovery.

Select the remote commitment claim from the existing pending sweeps
and assert that its outpoint is spent in the block. Keep the transaction
count, chain sync, channel-closure and balance checks.

Parse the claim with tag-independent harness and wire helpers so the
unit coverage build also compiles without the optional WalletKit tag.

commit.message:
itest: match RBF close updates to fee bump

The close stream can still contain Bob's initial low-fee offer when the
test expects his replacement. Receiving that event first fails the fee
assertion and leaves the next subtest with uncleared transactions.

Consume pending updates until Alice observes Bob's returned transaction
ID, then keep the existing fee, ownership and confirmation assertions.

Bound the whole match with the existing wait timeout. Return stream
errors from the predicate and keep assertions on the test goroutine.

commit.message:
itest: deflake outbound remote signer macaroon test

testOutboundRSMacaroonEnforcement waits a fixed 15 seconds for the
watch-only node to write its invoice macaroon. On slow CI runners with a
remote database backend, opening the database can take longer than that,
and the test fails with a missing macaroon file.

Wait for the macaroon with the default timeout, which already accounts
for remote database backends.

The watch-only node starts waiting for the signer after writing its
macaroons, and the test still has to open a stream and start the signer
node before the signer connects. Raise the watch-only node's signer
connection timeout to the default timeout as well, so a slow runner
doesn't move the flake to that step.

commit.message:
ci: bump gateway to v0.7.2 and skip comments from non-members

Bump the gateway-action and runtime pins to v0.7.2 together: the v0.7.2
runtime needs the job token that gateway-action v0.7.2 passes. The release
limits /gateway explain to maintainers and the PR author, authorizes every
command before any credential is loaded, and adds repeat guards for
explain (per finding) and check (per HEAD). Refused commands get no reply;
the reason is in the workflow log.

Also skip comments from anyone who is neither a repo/org member nor the PR
author, so they never boot a runner. The runtime still checks every
command's permission itself.

scripts: make OTS output deterministic for identical inputs

Keep the original CLI, dependencies, output layout and uploader behavior.
Fix the OTS subprocess hash seed, locale and timezone so identical responses
are traversed consistently. Sort proofs and replacement commands, omit local
backend details and generation times, and normalize output permissions.

Keep relative pending ages and transient diagnostics on the terminal rather
than in comparable files. Preserve the pending-age exit status.

commit.message:
scripts: add upgrade-ots.py

The OpenTimestamps proofs attached to releases are uploaded right after
stamping, when they still depend on the calendar servers. Once a
calendar has committed the stamp to Bitcoin, `ots upgrade` makes the
proof verifiable with a Bitcoin node alone.

upgrade-ots.py upgrades the proofs of the published releases that
aren't complete yet, verifies each upgraded proof against the release
file it timestamps, and writes the results to a new directory. It only
reads from GitHub. The directory holds upload.sh, which replaces the
proofs on the releases using gh, a summary, the upgraded proofs, the
originals as .ots.bak and the files they timestamp.

Proofs are verified with the local bitcoind by default. For testing
without a node, --esplora verifies them against block headers from an
Esplora API, and warns that this trusts that server.

commit.message:
actor: use t.Context in the parked Tell test

In this commit, we replace the two context.Background calls in
TestTellParkedBehindOverflowReturnsOnStop with t.Context, as the
usetesting linter asks. The test context stays live until the test
ends, so the external Tell still parks behind the overflow and the
late Tell still exercises the terminated actor.

docs: note the Drain race fix in the actor release note

In this commit, we extend the unreleased actor release note from #11431
to mention the Drain race fix in this PR. The overflow queue has not
shipped in a release yet, so the fix belongs next to the feature it
corrects rather than in a fragment of its own.

actor: hold overflowMu while Drain pops the overflow

In this commit, we fix a data race between ChannelMailbox.Drain and
the other readers of the overflow queue. Drain popped the queue with
popOverflowLocked without holding overflowMu, on the assumption that
nothing else touches the queue once the mailbox is closed. That
assumption does not hold. Send's wait loop takes overflowMu and reads
len(m.overflow) before it checks the closed flag, and OverflowLen
reads the same slice. A Send that arrives while the actor is shutting
down therefore races with Drain, and go test -race reports a write in
popOverflowLocked against a read in Send.

The race is benign in practice. The actor context is cancelled before
process() calls Close, so every interleaving ends with that Send
returning false. It is still a real race, and it makes the race
detector unusable for anything that sends during shutdown.

Drain now takes overflowMu around each pop only: lock, return if the
queue is empty, pop, unlock. The yield call stays outside the lock,
because process() sends to the dead letter office and completes
promises from it, and must not run under the mailbox lock. We also
correct the comments in Drain and on popOverflowLocked, since every
caller of the latter now holds overflowMu.

Two tests cover this. One drains a large overflow while another
goroutine calls OverflowLen and Send, and fails under -race without
the fix. The other checks at the Actor level that a Tell parked behind
a non-empty overflow returns after Stop, and that a Tell after Done
does not block.
